environment.description: Same application container image deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The task role has no relevant permissions beyond ECR pull and CloudWatch logs. The ALB target group has a response timeout of 5s. The critical control: the ECS task definition specifies a read-only root filesystem (readonlyRootFilesystem: true) and the container uses a tmpfs mount at /tmp only. The SQLite database path /var/lib/app/users.db is served from an EFS mount configured with an EFS Access Point that enforces POSIX permissions uid=1000, gid=1000 with permissions 0555 (read+execute only, no write). The EFS file system policy additionally denies efs:ClientWrite to all principals except a separate data-loader task role (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/data-loader-role). The application's task role (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/app-task-role) is explicitly denied efs:ClientWrite via a resource policy condition. Furthermore, the SQLite database file itself is opened by the application, but because the EFS mount is read-only at the filesystem level, any INSERT, UPDATE, or write operation (including the audit_log INSERT that precedes the vulnerable query) will cause sqlite3.OperationalError: attempt to write a readonly database, which triggers the except block and returns a 500 error BEFORE the injectable ORDER BY query is ever reached.

config.compute: ECS Fargate, task definition with readonlyRootFilesystem: true
